# LaminarDB

> LaminarDB is an open-source streaming SQL engine written in Rust (Apache-2.0). It reads events from sources such as Kafka, runs SQL continuously over them, and writes results to sinks or keeps them as queryable materialized views. It can be embedded in a Rust program (crate `laminar-db`) or run as a server (`laminardb` binary, Docker image `laminardb/laminardb-server`). The current packaged release is v0.33.0. LaminarDB is pre-1.0.

Key facts:

- SQL: `CREATE SOURCE`, `CREATE STREAM`, `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`, `CREATE SINK`. Event-time windows with `tumble`, `hop` and `session`; watermarks are declared on sources with `WATERMARK FOR ts AS ts - INTERVAL ...`; emit clauses include `EMIT ON WINDOW CLOSE` and `EMIT CHANGES`. Bounded interval joins, temporal joins and lookup tables are supported.
- Connectors in the default server build: Kafka (source and sink), PostgreSQL logical replication (source) and PostgreSQL (sink), MongoDB change streams (source) and MongoDB (sink), Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg (source and sink), NATS (source and sink), local files (source and sink), WebSocket and OpenTelemetry (best-effort only), and a built-in `generator` source. RabbitMQ, IBM MQ, FIX and FpML are optional build features: none is in the Docker image; the v0.33.0 x86_64 Linux (glibc) binary includes all four, the x86_64 Linux (musl) binary none, and the other binaries FIX and FpML.
- Delivery: at-least-once is the server default. Exactly-once needs a replayable source and a sink that commits with the checkpoint (for example Kafka input with Kafka, Delta Lake or Iceberg output in embedded and single-node mode). Single-node replayable delivery needs a local `file://` checkpoint.
- Deployment modes: embedded, single-node server, cluster. Cluster mode needs shared object-store checkpoints (S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure), accepts Kafka sources only, and rejects materialized views and AI functions.
- Server API: SQL over HTTP (`POST /api/v1/sql`, bearer `console_token`), WebSocket subscriptions (`/ws/{name}`), Prometheus metrics (`/metrics`), health probes (`/health`, `/ready`), optional PostgreSQL wire protocol (`pgwire_bind`).
- LaminarDB Console: a separate browser app (github.com/laminardb/laminardb-console-ui) for a server you run.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/laminardb/laminardb/blob/main/README.md): overview, quick start and examples
- [SQL reference](https://github.com/laminardb/laminardb/blob/main/docs/SQL_REFERENCE.md): streaming SQL syntax and mode-specific limits
- [Server configuration](https://laminardb.io/docs/): TOML keys, HTTP API and connector options
- [Connector guide](https://github.com/laminardb/laminardb/blob/main/crates/laminar-connectors/README.md): per-connector options and guarantees
- [Rust API](https://laminardb.io/api/laminar_db/): rustdoc for the crates on the main branch
- [Changelog](https://github.com/laminardb/laminardb/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Releases](https://github.com/laminardb/laminardb/releases)
